posts.title: Your Read Replica Did Not See the Save Yet
posts.summary: A commit on the primary and visibility on a read replica are different events. Return the committed view, route follow-up reads deliberately, or wait for a replica to reach a named consistency point when the product promises read-your-writes.

posts.title: Parallel Workers Can Overtake the Oldest Job
posts.summary: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED is a practical way for concurrent workers to claim different rows without waiting on each other. It also lets later jobs pass a locked earlier job, so FIFO order, fairness, and recovery need an explicit design outside the locking clause.

posts.title: A Full Connection Pool Is an Admission Decision You Did Not Make
posts.summary: When a database pool fills, its checkout queue quietly becomes an application scheduler. It usually knows nothing about request deadlines, tenants, route cost, or whether the caller still cares. Bound and classify database-bound work before the pool instead.

posts.title: The First Row May Not Be the First Fact
posts.summary: A larger auto-incrementing ID does not prove that its row committed later or represents a later business event. Decide which order a feature needs, then encode and enforce that order instead of inferring it from a primary key.

posts.title: Replaying a Dead-Letter Queue Is a New Production Change
posts.summary: A dead-letter replay is not a harmless undo of past failures. Repair the cause, select a bounded set, verify that current consumers can interpret old work, and observe redelivery as a new production change.

posts.title: A Lease Expiry Does Not Stop the Old Worker
posts.summary: Treat a distributed lease as a coordination signal, not a physical stop button. When a stale worker could still mutate shared state, send a monotonically increasing fencing token to the protected resource and make that resource reject superseded owners.

posts.title: Graceful Shutdown Starts by Refusing New Work
posts.summary: Graceful shutdown is an admission-control protocol, not just a signal handler. Stop accepting new requests or leases before draining active work, and budget for routing lag, long-lived connections, and the hard termination deadline.

posts.title: When a Commit and an Email Disagree
posts.summary: Avoid the dual write. Commit the business change and a durable outbox record together, then deliver asynchronously with a stable message identity, idempotent consumers, and an honest at-least-once contract.
